extracted_by: hand, T-0315 — the Democrat read, June 1834
note: Vol. I No. 27. Every column of this issue carries the Tesseract fallback banner, so the whole reading is the weaker of the two the segmenter offers. Pages 1-2 are poetry, a Peoria description and national and foreign reprint; the town is on the editorial half of page 2 column 4 and on pages 3 and 4, which are NOT interleaved in this issue — each segmenter column reads straight down one printed column. NO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST: all twenty-four columns were read, not searched. THIS IS THE SENIOR WITNESS to several advertisements the corpus already holds from their July reprints: Goss & Cobb's dateline is 'Chicago, June 4, 1834' and its insertion number 27 is this issue's, and A. Sweet's to-let building is dated May 6.

The Steam Boat Uncle Sam left Buffalo on Monday last agreeable to the arrangement. The Steam Boat Pioneer arrived here last evening, and will commence making regular tri[ps b]etween this and St. Joseph, for the seas[on. …] There are from four to five Schooners which [are] constantly plying across the [l]ak[e. …] The Stage has also commenced running twice a week to Niles.
claims.notes: THE TOWN'S TRAFFIC IN ONE PARAGRAPH, a year before the scene date: a Buffalo steamer weekly until 25 August, the Pioneer opening a St. Joseph ferry the evening before this issue, four or five schooners in constant lake service, and a stage twice a week to Niles. The lines are woven with the editorial above and below them and the quote takes only the ones that carry this notice.

claims.notes: ONE IMPRESSION OF THE STANDING LAKE STREET LAND-AGENCY CARD. The Democrat sets this advertisement, word for word the same, in every issue from 1834-05-14 to 1834-10-01 — twenty consecutive weeks, eighteen of which set the line ‘purchased and Sold, or by commi[s]sion’ recognisably (T-1051). The card is identified by its copy and not by its display line: the same trade (‘House and Land Agent’), the same offer of building lots in the town and the School Section, the same houses to let, and the same office on Lake street opposite Dr. Temple's. THIS IS THE IMPRESSION c008's OWN NOTE ALREADY CITES WITHOUT CLAIMING IT: the display line reads '@s DRANCRAID,' (line 2280), and that setting is one of the two the 1834-06-11 reading weighed when it supplied 'Wm. G. Branchaud'. It is claimed here so that the reading stands in the record and not only in another claim's prose. Nothing is read off the display line. THE PROPRIETOR'S NAME IS NOT READ HERE and none is supplied into the quote: the record's ‘W. G. Blanchard’ stands on T-0408's reading of the two impressions whose columns are NOT Tesseract fallbacks (1834-07-16 line 5527, 1834-09-17 line 3292) and on identity.json's declared firm merge, not on this impression. THE ADDRESS DOES NOT SURVIVE: the notice is cut at 'ths Office on' (line 2284) and neither the street nor the anchor is set, so this printing is recorded as silent about placement rather than given the address its neighbours print. The column is a Tesseract fallback (the flag is line 2279).
